lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Independent application: guardian review and attestation of real-world evidence

objective: Learners present their portfolio-in-progress to a guardian for a completeness-and-honesty review, so a second, trusted perspective checks the work before the final capstone defense, with the review scoped to completeness and honesty rather than judging the learner's chosen direction.
scenario: The learner presents their assembled portfolio index, plan statement, support-needs statement, and contingency branch to a guardian, who reviews it against a completeness checklist and attests that the review happened — explicitly not judging whether the learner's chosen direction is the 'right' one.
safetyNotes: The guardian review checks completeness and honesty against the checklist — it does not evaluate or approve the learner's chosen life direction, which remains the learner's own.
Any remaining gap named honestly during this review is a valid outcome, not a failure of the review.

simulationAlternative.description: If no guardian or trusted adult is available for a live review session today, the learner completes the same checklist as a structured self-review, flags any section they are unsure about, and schedules the guardian review for as soon as one is available; this self-review carries equal credit for completing today's lesson.

materials: the learner's assembled portfolio pieces from this unit

tasks.directions: Before the review, predict which piece your guardian will have the most questions about.

prompts.text: Which of your four assembled pieces do you predict your guardian (or the self-review checklist) will flag the most questions about, and why?

tasks.directions: Present the portfolio pieces for review and record the outcome.

prompts.text: I presented the portfolio index, plan statement, support-needs statement, and contingency branch for review.
The review (guardian or self-review) checked each piece against the completeness checklist.
What did the review find — fully complete, or one or more pieces still needing work? Record the outcome honestly, including any remaining gap.
How did it feel to have someone else check your plan for completeness, separate from whether they agreed with your direction?

remediation: If the review record claims full completeness with no gap at all, and that doesn't match what the earlier portfolio-index lesson honestly identified, reteach by having the learner reconcile the two — either the gap was genuinely closed since then, or it should still be named honestly here.
extension: Have the learner write one sentence describing what they would want a reviewer to ask them at the final capstone defense, based on what came up in this review.
